objects.description: Represents a Catch2 test session controller. It is non-copyable and coordinates command-line parsing, configuration, and executing tests. Provides APIs to set/parse configuration, run tests, and access the CLI parser and config. Internally owns a Clara::Parser, configuration data, and a unique_ptr to Config. Non-public lifecycle details (construction/destruction) are declared here and defined elsewhere.

Header-defined integral constants representing standard exit codes used by Catch2 sessions. They are constexpr ints in namespace Catch for various outcomes (e.g., general error, no tests run, unmatched test spec, all skipped, invalid spec, and test failure). Note: These are constants, not user-defined types.

Processed form of a ReporterSpec with defaults filled in. Holds reporter name, output filename, chosen colour mode, and custom options map. Equality is defined via the friend operator== declared here (implementation external).

Aggregated configuration values for a Catch2 test run, with defaults pre-set. Holds listing flags, runtime behavior flags, random seed, sharding info, benchmark settings, verbosity and reporting options, selection filters, and the premature-exit guard path.

Concrete implementation of Catch2's IConfig interface. Wraps ConfigData, computes derived data such as processed reporter specs and TestSpec, and exposes configuration to the framework and reporters. Constructible default or from provided ConfigData; destructor defined in the implementation file.

A value-comparison helper used in Catch2 assertions for approximate floating-point comparisons. It stores a target value, epsilon, margin, and scale, and defines comparison operators that consider these tolerances. Users can adjust epsilon, margin, and scale, and create customized instances. Details of comparison algorithm and validation are in private methods declared here and defined elsewhere.
Specialization of Catch2's StringMaker for Catch::Approx, enabling conversion of Approx instances to string form for reporting. Only declaration is provided here; definition is elsewhere.
Dummy struct in the global namespace used to enable bringing a matching global operator<< into Catch namespace for ADL of stream insertion checks.

Struct holding Catch2 library version components (major, minor, patch, optional branch name, and build number). Copy and assignment are disabled. It provides a constructor taking all components and a friend stream insertion operator for formatted output. The header declares, but does not define, the constructor and operator<<; their implementations are expected elsewhere. The free function libraryVersion() returns a const reference to a singleton Version instance owned by the library.

import random
from typing import List

# This generator produces a byte buffer intended to be interpreted by FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# calls in the provided fuzz stubs. The stubs choose argc in range [0,4] and then
# obtain up to 4 strings. We therefore encode a small container format that holds
# between 0 and 4 argv strings, each null-terminated, within a single byte buffer.
#
# Format:
#   [1 byte] count N (0..4)
#   then N arguments, each encoded as:
#       [1 byte] length L (0..250), number of following bytes of content
#       [L bytes] content (UTF-8 text)
#       [1 byte] NUL terminator (0x00) to satisfy C-string expectations
# Any remaining bytes are ignored by the consumer, but we keep output <= 4 KiB.
#
# The arguments are generated from a corpus of valid Catch2 CLI options and
# interesting values to drive different code paths in applyCommandLine/run.

_CATCH_FLAGS = [
    # Listing and help
    "--list-tests",
    "--list-tags",
    "--list-reporters",
    "--list-listeners",
    "-h",
    "--help",
    # Visibility/verbosity
    "-s",  # show successful tests
    "-v", "--verbosity",
    "--durations",  # requires arg: yes/no/always
    "--success",
    "--reporter",  # requires arg
    "-r",          # requires arg (alias)
    # Filters and names
    "-c",  # sections to run (requires arg)
    "-t",  # tags expression (requires arg)
    "--name",  # requires arg
    # Run order, random seed
    "-rng-seed",  # requires arg
    "--order",    # name or lex or random
    # Output & color
    "-o", "--out",  # requires arg
    "--colour", "--color",  # auto/yes/no
    # Abort/throw control
    "-x",            # abort after N failures (requires arg)
    "-e",            # no throw (negates allowThrows)
    "--break",       # break into debugger
    # Sharding
    "--shard-count",  # requires arg
    "--shard-index",  # requires arg
    # Benchmarks
    "--benchmark-no-analysis",
    "--benchmark-samples",           # requires arg
    "--benchmark-confidence-interval",  # requires arg
    "--benchmark-resamples",         # requires arg
    "--benchmark-warmup-time",       # requires arg (ms)
]

# Value pools for flags that take arguments
_REPORTERS = ["console", "compact", "junit", "xml", "tap", "sonarqube"]
_VERBOSITY = ["quiet", "normal", "high"]
_DURATIONS = ["no", "yes", "always"]
_BOOL = ["yes", "no", "true", "false", "1", "0"]
_ORDER = ["name", "lex", "random"]
_COLOUR = ["auto", "yes", "no"]
_NUMS = ["0", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "10", "42", "100", "1000", "100000"]
_SEEDS = ["1", "2", "3", "1337", "314159", "424242", "123456789"]
# Some representative tag/test spec expressions and sections
_SPECS = [
    "[fast]",
    "[slow]",
    "[!benchmark]",
    "tag1,tag2",
    "~[flaky]",
    "foo*",
    "FooBar",
]
_SECTIONS = ["init", "processing", "cleanup", "edge-cases"]
_NAMES = ["run-A", "nightly", "CI", "local", "shard-test"]
_OUTS = ["-", "report.txt", "results.xml", "out.tap", "stdout", "stderr"]

# Some compound argv sets that are known-valid and exercise multiple behaviors
_PRESETS: List[List[str]] = [
    ["--list-tests"],
    ["--list-tags"],
    ["-h"],
    ["-s", "--success"],
    ["-r", "junit", "-o", "results.xml"],
    ["--reporter", "compact", "--colour", "yes"],
    ["--order", "random", "-rng-seed", "1337"],
    ["--name", "CI", "-t", "[fast]"],
    ["--shard-count", "4", "--shard-index", "1"],
    ["--benchmark-no-analysis"],
]

# Choose if a flag requires an argument and supply it
def _arg_for_flag(rng: random.Random, flag: str) -> List[str]:
    if flag in ("-r", "--reporter"):
        return [flag, rng.choice(_REPORTERS)]
    if flag in ("-v", "--verbosity"):
        return [flag, rng.choice(_VERBOSITY)]
    if flag == "--durations":
        return [flag, rng.choice(_DURATIONS)]
    if flag in ("-t",):
        return [flag, rng.choice(_SPECS)]
    if flag in ("-c",):
        return [flag, rng.choice(_SECTIONS)]
    if flag == "--name":
        return [flag, rng.choice(_NAMES)]
    if flag in ("-o", "--out"):
        return [flag, rng.choice(_OUTS)]
    if flag == "-rng-seed":
        return [flag, rng.choice(_SEEDS)]
    if flag == "--order":
        return [flag, rng.choice(_ORDER)]
    if flag in ("--colour", "--color"):
        return [flag, rng.choice(_COLOUR)]
    if flag in ("-x", "--shard-count", "--shard-index", "--benchmark-samples",
                "--benchmark-resamples", "--benchmark-warmup-time"):
        return [flag, rng.choice(_NUMS)]
    if flag == "--benchmark-confidence-interval":
        # Use a few typical CI values
        return [flag, rng.choice(["0.80", "0.90", "0.95", "0.99"])]
    # Flags without args
    return [flag]

# Build up to 4 argv strings; include program name sometimes
def _build_argv(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # With some probability, pick a known-good preset truncated to <=4
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        preset = rng.choice(_PRESETS)
        # Optionally prepend a program name-like token
        argv = []
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            argv.append(rng.choice(["testbin", "catch2", "t"]))
        argv.extend(preset)
        return argv[:4]

    # Otherwise, synthesize arguments
    argv: List[str] = []
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        argv.append(rng.choice(["tests", "prog", "a.out"]))
    # Choose 1-3 flags and expand with args as needed, but cap total elements to 4
    flags = rng.sample(_CATCH_FLAGS, k=rng.randint(1, 3))
    for f in flags:
        if len(argv) >= 4:
            break
        parts = _arg_for_flag(rng, f)
        for p in parts:
            if len(argv) >= 4:
                break
            argv.append(p)
        if len(argv) >= 4:
            break
    # If still empty, add a generic token
    if not argv:
        argv.append("prog")
    return argv[:4]

# Encode argv into the simple binary container described above
def _encode_argv(argv: List[str]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    n = min(len(argv), 4)
    out.append(n & 0xFF)
    for s in argv[:n]:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        # Limit per-arg length to 250 to keep total under 4 KiB
        L = min(len(b), 250)
        out.append(L & 0xFF)
        out.extend(b[:L])
        out.append(0)  # NUL terminator
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    argv = _build_argv(rng)
    return _encode_argv(argv)

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for free-form text strings consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME in stubs
# Targeted to Catch2-related stubs that expect short names, filenames, reporter names, and
# general strings for stringification utilities. We compose argv-like options, small names,
# reporter specs, and printable/control mixes. The output is a single bytes buffer from which
# the fuzzer infra will slice for multiple FUZZ_PARAM_* calls.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

REPORTERS = [
    "console", "compact", "junit", "xml", "tap", "teamcity", "sonarqube",
]
COLOUR_MODES = ["auto", "yes", "no", "ansi", "win32", "disabled"]

# A small corpus of Catch2 CLI flags that are valid/interesting
CATCH_FLAGS = [
    "--list-tests", "--list-tags", "--list-reporters", "--list-listeners",
    "--success", "--durations=yes", "--durations=no", "--durations=always",
    "--rng-seed", "--order=lex", "--order=decl", "--order=rand",
    "--shard-count", "--shard-index", "--reporter", "--out",
    "--name", "--allow-running-no-tests", "--invisibles",
    "--benchmark-no-analysis", "--benchmark-samples", "--benchmark-resamples",
    "--benchmark-confidence-interval", "--benchmark-warmup-time",
]

# Some tag/test specs
TEST_SPECS = [
    "[fast]", "[slow]", "~[.benchmark]", "math/*", "~[flaky]",
    "Case Sensitive", "Section::Name", "tag1,tag2", "foo|bar",
]

ASCII_SAFE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ .:/\\"

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]

def _rand_word(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_SAFE) for _ in range(n))

def _bounded(rng: random.Random, s: str, cap: int) -> str:
    if len(s) <= cap:
        return s
    # Prefer to keep beginning and end parts sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.4 and cap >= 3:
        head = cap // 2
        tail = cap - head
        return s[:head] + s[-tail:]
    return s[:cap]

def _make_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create plausible filenames, possibly with directories and extensions
    parts = []
    depth = rng.randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(_rand_word(rng, 1, 8))
    base = _rand_word(rng, 1, 12)
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        ext = _rand_choice(rng, [".txt", ".log", ".xml", ".json", ".out", ".dat"])
    else:
        ext = ""
    parts.append(base + ext)
    path = "/".join(parts)
    # Occasionally generate Windows-like path
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        drive = chr(ord('C') + rng.randrange(3)) + ":\\"
        path = drive + path.replace('/', '\\')
    return _bounded(rng, path, 64)

def _make_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Small names for cfg.name/processName
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Phrase-like
        w = [_rand_word(rng, 2, 8).capitalize() for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
        return _bounded(rng, " ".join(w), 64)
    return _bounded(rng, _rand_word(rng, 3, 20), 64)

def _make_custom_option_kv(rng: random.Random):
    k = _bounded(rng, _rand_word(rng, 1, 12), 32)
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        v = _bounded(rng, _rand_word(rng, 0, 24), 64)
    else:
        v = _bounded(rng, _rand_choice(rng, ["true", "false", "1", "0", "verbose", "quiet"]), 64)
    return k, v

def _emit_kv_lines(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    for _ in range(count):
        k, v = _make_custom_option_kv(rng)
        lines.append(f"{k}={v}")
    return lines

def _with_controls(rng: random.Random, s: str, max_extra: int = 8) -> str:
    # Insert some control characters to exercise escapeInvisibles path
    controls = ['\t', '\n', '\r', '\x00', '\x1b']
    n = rng.randint(0, max_extra)
    out = list(s)
    for _ in range(n):
        pos = rng.randrange(len(out) + 1) if out else 0
        out.insert(pos, rng.choice(controls))
    return ''.join(out)

def _build_argv_block(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Construct a plausible CLI segment for applyCommandLine usage
    tokens = []
    # Program name
    tokens.append(_make_filename(rng))

    # Add a few flags with arguments
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 8)):
        flag = _rand_choice(rng, CATCH_FLAGS)
        tokens.append(flag)
        if flag in ("--rng-seed", "--shard-count", "--shard-index",
                    "--benchmark-samples", "--benchmark-resamples"):
            tokens.append(str(rng.randint(0, 100000)))
        elif flag == "--benchmark-confidence-interval":
            tokens.append(f"{rng.uniform(0.1, 0.999):.3f}")
        elif flag == "--benchmark-warmup-time":
            tokens.append(str(rng.randint(1, 10000)))
        elif flag in ("--reporter",):
            tokens.append(_rand_choice(rng, REPORTERS))
        elif flag in ("--out",):
            tokens.append(_make_filename(rng))
        elif flag in ("--name",):
            tokens.append(_make_name(rng))
    # Add some test specs
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        tokens.append(_rand_choice(rng, TEST_SPECS))
    s = " ".join(tokens)
    return _bounded(rng, s, 1024)

def _build_reporter_block(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mimic ProcessedReporterSpec content as text
    name = _rand_choice(rng, REPORTERS)
    outfn = _make_filename(rng)
    colour = _rand_choice(rng, COLOUR_MODES)
    kvs = _emit_kv_lines(rng, rng.randint(1, 3))
    lines = [
        f"reporter:{name}",
        f"output:{outfn}",
        f"colour:{colour}",
    ] + kvs
    s = "\n".join(lines)
    return _bounded(rng, s, 256)

def _build_stringify_block(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose a string with numbers, words, and escapes to feed stringify paths
    parts = []
    parts.append(str(rng.randint(-2**31, 2**31 - 1)))
    parts.append(f"{rng.uniform(-1e6, 1e6):.10g}")
    parts.append(_with_controls(rng, _rand_word(rng, 5, 20)))
    parts.append('"quoted"')
    s = " ".join(parts)
    return _bounded(rng, s, 1024)

def _build_general_blob(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Mix several blocks separated by NULs to allow parsers to split
    sections: List[bytes] = []
    # Names for cfg.name/processName
    sections.append(_make_name(rng).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    sections.append(_make_name(rng).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    # Reporter block
    sections.append(_build_reporter_block(rng).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    # CLI argv-like block
    sections.append(_build_argv_block(rng).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    # Stringify-focused block
    sections.append(_build_stringify_block(rng).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    # Add a few filenames
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        sections.append(_make_filename(rng).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    # Join with NUL separators and sprinkle some random bytes header for FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
    blob = b"\x00".join(sections)
    # Prepend some deterministic integers to satisfy multiple FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) usages
    ints = [
        rng.getrandbits(32), rng.getrandbits(32), rng.getrandbits(32), rng.getrandbits(32),
        rng.getrandbits(32), rng.getrandbits(32),
    ]
    header = b"".join(struct.pack("<I", x) for x in ints)
    out = header + blob
    return out[:MAX_TOTAL]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Create a composite buffer tailored for all targeted stubs
    data = _build_general_blob(rng)
    # Ensure non-empty and within bounds
    if not data:
        data = b"default\x00console\x00--list-tests"
    return data[:MAX_TOTAL]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: arbitrary bytes as C-string
# Used by stub:
#   std::string src = FUZZ_PARAM_STR();
# The stub then uses src.c_str() with n up to src.size()+5 and asserts
# len == min(n, src.size()). This relies on src being a valid C-string
# whose first NUL is at the end of the string buffer (i.e., no embedded NULs),
# because std::string::size() returns visible characters before the implicit
# trailing NUL. If we included embedded NULs, strlen(src.c_str()) would be
# less than src.size() and the assertion would fail. Therefore we must
# generate strings without embedded NUL. Any other bytes are fine.
#
# This generator returns a bytes object intended to be consumed by the harness
# as the initial buffer for FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. It encodes
# a variety of interesting, yet valid, C-strings without embedded NULs:
#  - ASCII printable sequences
#  - Sequences with control characters except NUL (e.g., \t, \n, \r, \x01)
#  - Long boundary near 0, 1, 2, 3, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 512, 1024
#  - Repeated characters, alternating patterns, random mixes
#  - Strings that look like options or file paths (for broader reuse)
#
# The function is deterministic for a given seed but provides variety.

PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "

# Control bytes excluding NUL (0x00)
CONTROL_BYTES = bytes([i for i in range(1, 32)]) + bytes([127])

# Safe byte choices for this stub: anything except 0x00
SAFE_BYTE_VALUES = bytes([i for i in range(1, 256)])

BOUNDARY_LENGTHS = [
    0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 95, 96, 127, 128,
    191, 192, 255, 256, 384, 512, 768, 1023, 1024
]


def _rand_printable(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return ("".join(r.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n))).encode("utf-8", "strict")


def _rand_controls(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix common controls with others (excluding NUL)
    common = b"\t\n\r\x01\x02\x1b"  # tab, newline, carriage return, SOH, STX, ESC
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(n):
        if r.random() < 0.5 and common:
            out.append(r.choice(list(common)))
        else:
            out.append(r.choice(list(CONTROL_BYTES)))
    return bytes(out)


def _rand_safe_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.choice(SAFE_BYTE_VALUES) for _ in range(n))


def _pattern_repeat(byte_val: int, n: int) -> bytes:
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    return bytes([byte_val]) * n


def _pattern_alternate(b1: int, b2: int, n: int) -> bytes:
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    arr = bytearray()
    for i in range(n):
        arr.append(b1 if (i % 2 == 0) else b2)
    return bytes(arr)


def _looks_like_path(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Generate POSIX-like or Windows-like paths without NULs
    if n == 0:
        return b""
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        # POSIX
        parts = []
        remaining = n
        while remaining > 0:
            seg_len = max(1, min(remaining, r.randint(1, 10)))
            seg = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_._") for _ in range(seg_len))
            parts.append(seg)
            remaining -= seg_len
            if remaining > 0:
                parts.append('/')
                remaining -= 1
        s = ''.join(parts)
        return s.encode('utf-8')[:n]
    else:
        # Windows
        drive = r.choice(string.ascii_uppercase) + ":\\"
        remaining = max(0, n - len(drive))
        parts = [drive]
        while remaining > 0:
            seg_len = max(1, min(remaining, r.randint(1, 10)))
            seg = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_._") for _ in range(seg_len))
            parts.append(seg)
            remaining -= seg_len
            if remaining > 0:
                parts.append('\\')
                remaining -= 1
        s = ''.join(parts)
        return s.encode('utf-8')[:n]


def _looks_like_cli(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Create CLI-like arguments string (single buffer) without NULs
    flags = ["-v", "-s", "-a", "-b", "--list-tests", "--list-tags", "--reporter", "--success"]
    args = []
    while True:
        if len(' '.join(args)) >= n or not flags:
            break
        f = r.choice(flags)
        flags.remove(f)
        args.append(f)
        if r.random() < 0.6 and len(' '.join(args)) < n:
            val_len = r.randint(1, max(1, min(12, n - len(' '.join(args)))))
            val = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.:/") for _ in range(val_len))
            args.append(val)
        if len(' '.join(args)) >= n:
            break
    s = ' '.join(args)
    if len(s) < n:
        # pad with random printable chars
        s += ''.join(r.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n - len(s)))
    return s.encode('utf-8')[:n]


def _choose_length(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias towards boundary sizes but allow random in [0, 1024]
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        L = r.choice(BOUNDARY_LENGTHS)
    else:
        L = r.randint(0, 1024)
    # Ensure max 1024 per stub's own cap; overall limit 4096 anyway
    return min(L, 1024)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    length = _choose_length(r)

    # Choose a content strategy
    strategies = [
        "printable", "controls", "safe_random", "repeat", "alternate",
        "path", "cli", "mixed"
    ]
    strat = r.choice(strategies)

    if strat == "printable":
        data = _rand_printable(r, length)
    elif strat == "controls":
        data = _rand_controls(r, length)
    elif strat == "safe_random":
        data = _rand_safe_bytes(r, length)
    elif strat == "repeat":
        b = r.choice(SAFE_BYTE_VALUES)
        data = _pattern_repeat(b, length)
    elif strat == "alternate":
        b1 = r.choice(SAFE_BYTE_VALUES)
        b2 = r.choice(SAFE_BYTE_VALUES)
        # Avoid identical bytes
        if b1 == b2:
            b2 = (b2 % 255) + 1
        data = _pattern_alternate(b1, b2, length)
    elif strat == "path":
        data = _looks_like_path(r, length)
    elif strat == "cli":
        data = _looks_like_cli(r, length)
    else:  # mixed
        # Compose segments of different types
        remaining = length
        parts: List[bytes] = []
        builders = [
            lambda k: _rand_printable(r, k),
            lambda k: _rand_controls(r, k),
            lambda k: _rand_safe_bytes(r, k),
        ]
        while remaining > 0:
            k = r.randint(1, max(1, min(32, remaining)))
            parts.append(r.choice(builders)(k))
            remaining -= k
        data = b"".join(parts)

    # Ensure no embedded NULs; replace any accidental 0x00 with 0x01
    if data:
        data = data.replace(b"\x00", b"\x01")

    # Limit to 4096 just in case (though we cap earlier)
    return data[:4096]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: nullable C-string
# The fuzz stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain a std::string that is then
# used as a C string (char const* / char*), truncated to 1024 bytes and
# required to be null-terminated when passed as char*.
# Our job: generate a bytes buffer from which the harness will draw, ideally
# yielding interesting but valid strings. We cannot control the harness directly,
# but typically FUZZ_PARAM_STR() slices bytes to a string; we thus provide
# diverse, valid textual payloads including edge cases and varied encodings.

# We will produce a single bytes blob that contains one chosen scenario payload.
# Harnesses commonly read sequentially; even if they split, each payload here is
# self-contained, valid as a C-string (no embedded NUL unless intended). We keep
# size <= 4096.

ASCII_PRINTABLE = ''.join(chr(i) for i in range(32, 127))
WHITESPACE = "\t\n\r \v\f"
PUNCT = string.punctuation

# A set of interesting Unicode sequences encoded in UTF-8
UNICODE_SNIPPETS = [
    "π≈3.14159",
    "こんにちは世界",
    "😀😇🙃😉",
    "naïve façade coöperate soufflé",
    "русский текст",
    "عربى نص",
    "हिन्दी परीक्षण",
    "韩文混合English",
]

# Strings that resemble CLI options used by Catch2 to explore different code paths
CATCH_CLI_SNIPPETS = [
    "--help",
    "-h",
    "--list-tests",
    "--list-tags",
    "--list-reporters",
    "--success",
    "--reporter junit",
    "--reporter console",
    "--rng-seed 12345",
    "--shard-count 4 --shard-index 2",
    "-r xml -o results.xml",
    "--colour-mode ansi",
    "--durations yes",
    "[tag1][tag2]",
    "TestCaseName",
]

# Edge-case generators

def gen_empty() -> bytes:
    return b""


def gen_ascii_random(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 0, max_len: int = 1024) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Include spaces, punctuation, digits, letters
    pool = ASCII_PRINTABLE
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(n))
    return s.encode('utf-8')


def gen_whitespace_heavy(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(1, 1024)
    pool = WHITESPACE
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(n))
    return s.encode('ascii')


def gen_unicode_mixture(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts: List[str] = []
    k = rng.randint(1, 6)
    for _ in range(k):
        choice = rng.randint(0, 3)
        if choice == 0:
            parts.append(''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 40))))
        elif choice == 1:
            parts.append(rng.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS))
        else:
            # Compose combining marks randomly
            base = rng.choice("aeiouyAEIOUY")
            combining = '\u0301\u0302\u0308\u030A\u0327\u0332'
            parts.append(base + ''.join(rng.choice(combining) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4))))
    s = ' '.join(parts)
    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 1024:
        b = b[:1024]
    return b


def gen_cli_like(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a plausible CLI line with mixed options and names
    parts: List[str] = []
    count = rng.randint(1, 6)
    for _ in range(count):
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            parts.append(rng.choice(CATCH_CLI_SNIPPETS))
        else:
            # Random arg
            token_len = rng.randint(1, 32)
            token = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '-_./:') for _ in range(token_len))
            parts.append(token)
    s = ' '.join(parts)
    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 1024:
        b = b[:1024]
    return b


def gen_path_like(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Generate filename/path-like string
    parts = []
    depth = rng.randint(1, 6)
    for _ in range(depth):
        seg_len = rng.randint(1, 16)
        seg = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ .") for _ in range(seg_len)).strip()
        if not seg:
            seg = "segment"
        parts.append(seg)
    path = '/'.join(parts)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        path += ".xml"
    elif rng.random() < 0.6:
        path += ".txt"
    b = path.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 1024:
        b = b[:1024]
    return b


def gen_numeric_series(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Series of numbers separated by spaces/commas
    nums = []
    count = rng.randint(1, 200)
    for _ in range(count):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            nums.append(str(rng.randint(-10**9, 10**9)))
        else:
            # floats with various precisions
            val = rng.uniform(-1e6, 1e6)
            prec = rng.randint(0, 12)
            nums.append(f"{val:.{prec}f}")
    sep = rng.choice([" ", ",", ";", " | "])
    s = sep.join(nums)
    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 1024:
        b = b[:1024]
    return b


def gen_edge_cases(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    cases = [
        b"-", b"--", b"-0", b"0", b"+0",
        b"true", b"false",
        b"NaN", b"inf", b"-inf",
        b"\"quoted\"",
        b"{ a, b, c }",
        b"[section][tag]",
        b"#include <catch2/catch.hpp>",
    ]
    s = rng.choice(cases)
    extra = b""
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        extra = b" " + gen_ascii_random(rng, 0, 64)
    b = s + extra
    if len(b) > 1024:
        b = b[:1024]
    return b


def gen_long_repetitions(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    token = rng.choice(["A", "0", " ", "-", "x", "\t"])  # simple chars
    n = rng.randint(1, 1024)
    b = (token * n).encode('ascii')
    return b


def maybe_embed_nul(rng: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # For const char*: embedded NUL will truncate; still valid. We sometimes
    # inject a NUL in the middle to test truncation logic in string conversion.
    if not data:
        return data
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        pos = rng.randint(0, min(len(data)-1, 256))
        return data[:pos] + b"\x00" + data[pos+1:]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    gens = [
        gen_empty,
        lambda: gen_ascii_random(rng, 0, 1024),
        lambda: gen_whitespace_heavy(rng),
        lambda: gen_unicode_mixture(rng),
        lambda: gen_cli_like(rng),
        lambda: gen_path_like(rng),
        lambda: gen_numeric_series(rng),
        lambda: gen_edge_cases(rng),
        lambda: gen_long_repetitions(rng),
    ]
    g = rng.choice(gens)
    data = g()

    # Optionally embed a NUL to exercise C-string truncation behavior for char const*
    data = maybe_embed_nul(rng, data)

    # Ensure total size <= 4096
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]

    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets identifier/name-like strings used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR in the
# ProcessedReporterSpec fuzzer stub. The stub expects multiple strings:
# - reporter name (<= 64 chars)
# - output filename (<= 64 chars)
# - three custom option keys (<= 32 chars each)
# - three custom option values (<= 64 chars each)
# The fuzzer harness will read these sequentially via FUZZ_PARAM_STR, so we provide
# them concatenated with null-termination to mimic C-string boundaries. We keep
# them valid and varied to exercise different code paths while staying reasonable.

MAX_TOTAL_SIZE = 4096

# Some interesting reporter names typically recognized by Catch2 or common patterns
KNOWN_REPORTER_NAMES = [
    "console",
    "compact",
    "junit",
    "xml",
    "tap",
    "sonarqube",
    "teamcity",
    "csv",
    "automake",
    "minimal",
]

# Common file extensions for report outputs
OUTPUT_EXTS = [".txt", ".log", ".xml", ".junit.xml", ".tap", ".csv"]

# Some interesting custom option keys that reporters might parse
KNOWN_OPTION_KEYS = [
    "colour-mode",
    "color-mode",
    "use-colour",
    "use-color",
    "filenames-as-tags",
    "durations",
    "verbosity",
    "reporter",
    "out",
    "locale",
]

# Values for options
BOOLS = ["true", "false", "1", "0", "yes", "no", "on", "off"]
VERBOSITIES = ["quiet", "normal", "high"]
DURATIONS = ["never", "always", "onError", "default", "detailed"]
COLOURS = ["auto", "yes", "no", "ansi", "win32"]

SAFE_IDENT_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_./@#:+,"
SAFE_KEY_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.:/@#,+"
SAFE_VAL_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " -_./:@#,+=()[]{}" + "\t"


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, max_len: int, base_pool: str = SAFE_IDENT_CHARS) -> str:
    # Ensure at least 1 char; prefer readable identifiers with optional slashes/dots
    n = rng.randint(1, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(base_pool) for _ in range(n))


def _choose_weighted(rng: random.Random, choices: List[str], p_known: float, fallback_max: int) -> str:
    if rng.random() < p_known and choices:
        return rng.choice(choices)
    return _rand_ident(rng, fallback_max)


def _make_filename(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    # Compose directory parts and a basename with extension
    parts = []
    # 0-2 directories
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
        parts.append(_rand_ident(rng, rng.randint(1, 10), base_pool=string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"))
    base = _rand_ident(rng, rng.randint(3, 16), base_pool=string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_")
    ext = rng.choice(OUTPUT_EXTS)
    path = "/".join(parts + [base + ext]) if parts else base + ext
    if len(path) > max_len:
        path = path[:max_len]
    return path


def _make_option_key(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 32) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        key = rng.choice(KNOWN_OPTION_KEYS)
    else:
        key = _rand_ident(rng, rng.randint(3, max_len), base_pool=SAFE_KEY_CHARS)
    return key[:max_len]


def _make_option_value(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    # Prefer meaningful values, otherwise random but readable text
    r = rng.random()
    if r < 0.25:
        val = rng.choice(BOOLS)
    elif r < 0.45:
        val = rng.choice(VERBOSITIES)
    elif r < 0.65:
        val = rng.choice(DURATIONS)
    elif r < 0.85:
        val = rng.choice(COLOURS)
    else:
        # Generate a sentence-like value
        words = [
            _rand_ident(rng, rng.randint(2, 8), base_pool=string.ascii_lowercase)
            for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5))
        ]
        val = " ".join(words)
    # Occasionally numeric values
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        val = str(rng.randint(0, 100000))
    return val[:max_len]


def _null_terminate(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Ensure no embedded nulls; replace them to keep validity
    if "\x00" in s:
        s = s.replace("\x00", " ")
    return s.encode("utf-8", errors="replace") + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Reporter name (<= 64): mix known names with random identifiers
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        name = rng.choice(KNOWN_REPORTER_NAMES)
        # Sometimes decorate with prefix/suffix to explore aliasing
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            name = (rng.choice(["default-", "custom-", "user-"]) + name)[:64]
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            name = (name + rng.choice(["-v1", "-v2", "-dbg"]))[:64]
    else:
        name = _rand_ident(rng, rng.randint(3, 64))
    name = name[:64]

    # Output filename (<= 64): generate path-like with known extensions
    out_fn = _make_filename(rng, 64)

    # 3 key/value pairs
    kv = []
    for _ in range(3):
        k = _make_option_key(rng, 32)
        v = _make_option_value(rng, 64)
        kv.append((k, v))

    # Build the byte stream as a sequence of null-terminated strings consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    # Order in stub: name, outputFilename, k0, v0, k1, v1, k2, v2
    parts = []
    parts.append(_null_terminate(name))
    parts.append(_null_terminate(out_fn))
    for k, v in kv:
        parts.append(_null_terminate(k))
        parts.append(_null_terminate(v))

    blob = b"".join(parts)

    # Ensure within size limit
    if len(blob) > MAX_TOTAL_SIZE:
        blob = blob[:MAX_TOTAL_SIZE]
        # Ensure the buffer ends with a null terminator for safety
        if not blob.endswith(b"\x00"):
            blob = blob[:-1] + b"\x00"

    return blob

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for filename/path strings suitable for filesystem usage
# Target stub expects multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR used as:
# - reporter name (<=64)
# - output filename/path (<=64)  [filename/path data type]
# - map keys (<=32)
# - map values (<=64)
# It also consumes an unsigned int via FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) for colour mode selection.
# We will pack these sequentially into a single bytes buffer with length-prefixing so the
# fuzzer harness can split deterministically. We keep everything valid and within bounds.
#
# Binary layout (all little-endian):
#  [u32] colour_selector
#  [u8]  reporter_name_len  (<=64)
#  [bytes] reporter_name (UTF-8)
#  [u8]  output_filename_len (<=64)
#  [bytes] output_filename (UTF-8)
#  Repeat 3 times for customOptions pairs:
#    [u8] key_len (<=32)
#    [bytes] key (UTF-8)
#    [u8] val_len (<=64)
#    [bytes] val (UTF-8)
# Total size kept <= 4096.
#
# We generate path-like strings for output filename, human-ish reporter names, and
# reasonable keys/values to trigger map behavior (duplicates, empty, special chars).

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."
KEY_SAFE = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-_:."
VALUE_SAFE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ .,:/=+@#%[](){}"
PATH_SEP = "/"

REPORTER_NAMES = [
    "console", "compact", "junit", "xml", "tap", "teamcity", "sonarqube", "timeline",
    "verbose", "minimal", "custom", "pretty",
]

EXTS = [".txt", ".log", ".xml", ".json", ".tap", ".out", ""]
ROOTS = ["./", "../", "/tmp/", "/var/tmp/", "", ".cache/"]


def rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int, alphabet: str) -> str:
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def gen_reporter_name(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    # Mix of curated names and random tokens; ensure non-empty, <= max_len
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.5:
        name = rand_choice(rng, REPORTER_NAMES)
    else:
        # random identifier-like
        base = rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(4, min(12, max_len)), string.ascii_lowercase)
        suffixes = ["", "-reporter", "_rep", "-v", "2"]
        name = base + rand_choice(rng, suffixes)
    # Occasionally include namespace-like qualifier
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        name = f"{name}:{rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 5), string.ascii_lowercase)}"
    return name[:max_len] if len(name) > 0 else "console"


def gen_path_component(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Avoid empty and dot-only segments sometimes; include dots, dashes
    base_len = max(1, min(max_len, rng.randint(1, max_len)))
    s = rand_ascii(rng, base_len, SAFE_ASCII)
    # Trim spaces at ends for cleanliness
    return s.strip() or "file"


def gen_filename(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    # Generate a valid relative/absolute path under max_len
    root = rand_choice(rng, ROOTS)
    parts: List[str] = []
    # 0-3 subdirectories
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        parts.append(gen_path_component(rng, rng.randint(1, 10)))
    fname_base = gen_path_component(rng, rng.randint(1, 16))
    ext = rand_choice(rng, EXTS)
    candidate = root + PATH_SEP.join(parts + [fname_base + ext]) if parts else root + fname_base + ext
    # Ensure within bound; if too long, reduce components
    if len(candidate) > max_len:
        # fall back to short root and base
        short_root = "" if root.startswith("/") and len(root) > 1 else root
        fname_base = fname_base[: max(1, max_len - len(short_root) - len(ext))]
        candidate = short_root + fname_base + ext
        if len(candidate) == 0:
            candidate = "out.log"
    # Occasionally choose special filenames
    specials = ["-", "NUL", "CON", "AUX", "PRN"]
    if rng.random() < 0.05:
        candidate = rand_choice(rng, specials)
    return candidate[:max_len] or "out.log"


def gen_key(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 32) -> str:
    # Keys like option names; allow duplicates and empty sometimes
    p = rng.random()
    if p < 0.15:
        return ""  # empty key
    if p < 0.45:
        presets = ["color", "verbosity", "durations", "timestamps", "theme", "output"]
        k = rand_choice(rng, presets)
    else:
        k = rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, max_len), KEY_SAFE)
    return k[:max_len]


def gen_value(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    # Values can be booleans, integers, floats, enums, or free text
    t = rng.randrange(6)
    if t == 0:
        return rand_choice(rng, ["true", "false", "on", "off", "yes", "no"])[:max_len]
    if t == 1:
        return str(rng.randint(0, 1000000))[:max_len]
    if t == 2:
        return (f"{rng.uniform(-1e6, 1e6):.6g}")[:max_len]
    if t == 3:
        return rand_choice(rng, ["default", "detailed", "compact", "quiet", "normal"])[:max_len]
    if t == 4:
        # small path-like value
        return gen_filename(rng, max_len)
    # free text
    return rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, max_len), VALUE_SAFE)


def pack_u32_le(x: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((x & 0xFF, (x >> 8) & 0xFF, (x >> 16) & 0xFF, (x >> 24) & 0xFF))


def pack_u8(x: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((x & 0xFF,))


def encode_field(s: str, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')[:max_len]
    return pack_u8(len(b)) + b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:

    # Colour selector domain can be any u32; stub mods by 6
    colour = rng.getrandbits(32)

    reporter = gen_reporter_name(rng, 64)
    out_fn = gen_filename(rng, 64)

    # Generate 3 key/value pairs, with potential duplicates for map behavior
    k0, v0 = gen_key(rng, 32), gen_value(rng, 64)
    # Occasionally duplicate key or value
    if rng.random() < 0.3:

    else:

    if rng.random() < 0.2:

    elif rng.random() < 0.4:

    elif rng.random() < 0.4:

    else:

    parts = []
    parts.append(pack_u32_le(colour))
    parts.append(encode_field(reporter, 64))

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: key string
# Used by fuzzer stub to populate keys (k0, k1, k2) for customOptions map and also
# general strings for name and outputFilename. The stub truncates to bounds.
# We will generate a compact, structured payload that the harness splits into
# multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls deterministically. The harness usually
# consumes sequential slices from the provided buffer. We therefore encode
# a simple length-prefixed sequence of UTF-8 strings so each FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# read retrieves a valid short string.
#
# Goals:
# - Provide 8 short strings to cover: name, outputFilename, k0, v0, k1, v1, k2, v2
# - Keep keys key-like (alnum + [-_.:/]) and values more freeform text
# - Include interesting variations: empty, max length, unicode, punctuation
# - Stay <= 4096 bytes
#
# Encoding format:
# [magic 4 bytes] = b"KSTR"
# [count 1 byte] = number of strings N (we emit 8)
# For i in 0..N-1:
#   [len 1 byte] = L (0..64)  -- stub will further clamp but we keep <=64
#   [L bytes] UTF-8 string contents
# Remaining bytes can include small entropy to feed other FUZZ_PARAM types
# (e.g., unsigned int for colourMode), so we append 4 bytes of random data.
# This simple framing helps typical fuzz infra that slices FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# by reading framed chunks.

SAFE_KEY_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.:/@+#"
SAFE_VAL_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, s: str, n: int) -> str:
    return "".join(rng.choice(s) for _ in range(n))


def _make_key_variants(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    variants = []
    # 1) Empty key (edge case)
    variants.append("")
    # 2) Short alnum
    variants.append(_rand_choice(rng, string.ascii_lowercase, rng.randint(3, 8)))
    # 3) With punctuation
    variants.append(_rand_choice(rng, SAFE_KEY_CHARS, rng.randint(5, 16)))
    # 4) Path-like
    parts = [
        _rand_choice(rng, string.ascii_lowercase, rng.randint(2, 5)),
        _rand_choice(rng, string.ascii_lowercase, rng.randint(2, 5)),
    ]
    variants.append("/".join(parts))
    # 5) Namespaced key
    variants.append(_rand_choice(rng, string.ascii_lowercase, rng.randint(2, 5)) + ":" + _rand_choice(rng, string.ascii_lowercase, rng.randint(2, 6)))
    # 6) With separators
    variants.append(_rand_choice(rng, string.ascii_lowercase + "-_.", rng.randint(4, 20)))
    # 7) Uppercase + digits
    variants.append(_rand_choice(rng, string.ascii_uppercase + string.digits, rng.randint(4, 12)))
    # 8) Near max length
    variants.append(_rand_choice(rng, SAFE_KEY_CHARS, 32))
    return variants


def _make_value_variants(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    variants = []
    # 1) Empty value
    variants.append("")
    # 2) Simple word
    variants.append(_rand_choice(rng, string.ascii_lowercase, rng.randint(3, 10)))
    # 3) Sentence-like
    words = [
        _rand_choice(rng, string.ascii_lowercase, rng.randint(2, 8))
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5))
    ]
    variants.append(" ".join(words))
    # 4) Punctuation heavy
    variants.append(_rand_choice(rng, string.punctuation, rng.randint(5, 20)))
    # 5) Mixed
    variants.append(_rand_choice(rng, SAFE_VAL_CHARS, rng.randint(10, 30)))
    # 6) Unicode accents
    variants.append("café naïve résumé – αβγ")
    # 7) JSON-like
    variants.append('{"k": "v", "n": %d}' % rng.randint(0, 1000))
    # 8) Near max length
    variants.append(_rand_choice(rng, SAFE_VAL_CHARS, 64))
    return variants


def _make_name_variants(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    return [
        "",  # empty name
        "console",
        "xml",
        "junit",
        "compact",
        "tap",
        _rand_choice(rng, string.ascii_lowercase, rng.randint(3, 12)),
        _rand_choice(rng, string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_", rng.randint(8, 20)),
    ]


def _make_filename_variants(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    bases = [
        "",  # stdout
        "report.txt",
        "results.xml",
        "out.json",
        "logs/output.tap",
        _rand_choice(rng, string.ascii_lowercase, rng.randint(3, 8)) + ".txt",
        "./" + _rand_choice(rng, string.ascii_lowercase, rng.randint(3, 8)) + ".log",
        "/tmp/" + _rand_choice(rng, string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, rng.randint(4, 12)),
    ]
    return bases


def _pack_strings(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    out += b"KSTR"
    out.append(len(strings) & 0xFF)
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
        if len(b) > 64:
            b = b[:64]
        out.append(len(b) & 0xFF)
        out += b
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose variants deterministically from the seed
    name = rng.choice(_make_name_variants(rng))
    filename = rng.choice(_make_filename_variants(rng))

    keys = _make_key_variants(rng)
    vals = _make_value_variants(rng)

    # Select three key/value pairs ensuring keys are distinct to exercise map behavior
    rng.shuffle(keys)
    k0, k1, k2 = keys[:3]
    v0 = rng.choice(vals)
    v1 = rng.choice(vals)
    v2 = rng.choice(vals)

    strings = [name, filename, k0, v0, k1, v1, k2, v2]
    payload = _pack_strings(strings)

    # Append 4 bytes for an unsigned int domain used by colourMode selection in stub
    colour_sel = rng.getrandbits(32)
    payload += colour_sel.to_bytes(4, 'little')

    # Ensure size bound
    return payload[:4096]
